title: Choosing storage: UserDefaults, files, Keychain, SwiftData, Core Data, SQLite
summary: Pick storage by what you save: small settings → UserDefaults; secrets → Keychain; images and blobs → files; searchable related records → SwiftData / Core Data / SQLite.
body: **UserDefaults:** tiny key-value settings (theme, "onboarding seen"). Loaded into memory at launch - never store big data or secrets here.
**Keychain:** passwords, tokens, keys. Encrypted by the system, survives app reinstall.

**Files:** images, downloads, JSON caches. `Caches/` can be deleted by the system when space is low; `Application Support/` is kept and backed up (exclude big re-downloadable files from backup). Write atomically.
**SwiftData (iOS 17+):** `@Model` classes, `@Query` in SwiftUI, background work with `@ModelActor`. Easiest for new apps; less control for complex migrations and very large data.
**Core Data:** mature object graph framework - faulting (loads objects lazily), batch operations, CloudKit sync, migrations, history tracking. More code but more control.
**SQLite (often via GRDB):** plain SQL tables, predictable performance, full-text search; good for sync engines. You write more code.

**Data protection:** files can be encrypted until the user unlocks the device. The default (`completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`) is readable after first unlock; `.complete` is safer but unreadable in background while locked.
**Offline-first:** treat the local database as the source of truth for the UI and sync with the server in the background (see System Design: "Offline-first sync").
keyPoints: UserDefaults = small settings; Keychain = secrets; files = blobs; DB = structured, queryable data.
SwiftData for new SwiftUI apps; Core Data for mature/complex needs; SQLite/GRDB for full control.
Choose a data-protection class that matches background access needs.
Test migrations with real old stores from every shipped version.

mistakes: Storing tokens in UserDefaults (plain text in a plist).
Storing large arrays/images in UserDefaults (slows launch).
Doing big database work on the main context.
followups: **How do you handle a corrupt database?** Detect on open, move the file aside, recreate, resync from server, report the event.
**How do you share data with a widget?** App Group container (shared files, `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`, or a shared database).
